children.translated_text: The First Canto
Salutation to the lineage.
which has extended its expanse, unfathomably deep,
Bow down to that which has grown immeasurably tall,
which is manifestly the supreme reality of the beginningless — the slaying of <s>Madhu</s>,
whose surface is scarcely touched,
from whose flashing [weapon], cast aside with the splendor of the sky,
stained with the blood of the lord of <s>Dānavas</s>,
covering [herself], fell as though slipping from her breast-garment,
the beauty of the great <s>Asura</s>'s consort,
which was firmly grasped by the harsh ends of his arms,
the object of which is difficult to fathom even through satisfaction,
whose life was released with difficulty from the throat,
the neck of <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, twisted unevenly,
by whom, having gained strength from roots of firmly grown virtues,
who shook the girdle of the earth,
the fame of great <s>Indra</s> was shattered.
like an aerial root uprooting a tree,
Salutation to the lineage.
blazing with the fire of nine [emotions], kindled by the shadow of his throat,
Bow down also to him whose resounding voice,
like the sun of the directions, whose darkness above has been ignited,
flashes with a burst of laughter,
her limbs languid with breasts horripilated, she turns to embrace him,
whose [beloved], drawn close, trembles,
her left half eager for the going of the life-breath,
confused by the nature of love,
clearly echoed, slipping on the surfaces of the directions,
to whose [laughter] there cling in the sky,
splashes of laughter on the moon-white jeweled surfaces,
like waves of moonlight,
whose [oceans], with fish darting about in churning waves,
agitated by the commencement of the dance,
with the mouths of the submarine fire veiled by mist from the spray — [such are his] great ocean-jewels.
become [seas] with waters swelling,
standing firm on slippery, crumbling [ground],
Begun with fresh passion,
the tale of poetry is difficult to carry forth.
like friendship, delightful from the start,
fame is esteemed, virtues are displayed,
